subject: Security checks: transit & at-rest guardrails + architecture sketch
messages:

Subject: LumenRx procurement: PII transit/at-rest controls + sketch request

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As procurement/legal run the intake for our vendor security review, we need a concise response on Redwood's controls for the following high-level items:

- How PII is classified and isolated at rest (storage tiers, encryption-at-rest keys, KMS custody options).
- Transit protections across public cloud regions and any cross-border routing safeguards.
- Subprocessor roster and whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext PII or only telemetry/metrics.
- Retention defaults for inference logs and any customer-configurable retention windows.

Can you share a one-page architecture sketch (network boundaries + where KMS sits) and a procurement checklist we can attach to the review packet? If you have a short answers doc for our security questionnaire we can paste into our portal, that'd speed things up.

Procurement timeline: we need initial artifacts by COB Friday so Legal can proceed with an initial redline.

Thanks,

Sara Lopez
Senior Counsel, LumenRx
security@lumenrx.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: LumenRx procurement: PII transit/at-rest controls + sketch request

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching two artifacts: a one-page architecture sketch and a procurement checklist that maps to the items you listed. Quick summary below; the attachments have the exact wording you can paste into your portal.

Summary answers (short):
- At-rest classification: Customer PII is stored in tenant-scoped buckets/volumes with per-tenant keys. Default: AES-256 encryption using cloud KMS. Customers on Private/Dedicated can bring their own key (BYOK) or use HSM-backed KMS via our key proxy.
- Transit: Mutual TLS between customer gateway and Redwood edge. Internal service-to-service traffic is encrypted (mTLS) and segmented per-tenant. We also support region pinning to avoid unintended cross-border routing.
- Subprocessors: Most inference-serving infra is Redwood-managed subprocessor list; none are permitted to access customer plaintext PII unless explicitly contracted (e.g., managed migration). Enrollment and attestations are included in the checklist.
- Retention: Default inference telemetry retained 30 days; request logs (input tokens) default to 7 days unless Customer enables longer retention. All retention windows are configurable at the account level.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm the current subprocessor attestation pack link and whether EvidenceStore will host the artifacts?

Best,

Michael Grant

Michael / Kim — quick internal note before we publish:

- Subprocessors: current roster (infra + telemetry + storage) is v2027-06-01. None have access to plaintext inference inputs by default; only anonymized telemetry and aggregated metrics. We do have a managed-migration subprocessor (on rare customer request) that can be granted scoped access via an encrypted staging bucket and short-lived credentials — this is called out in the checklist with a required POA and dual-signer attestation.
- KMS custody: for Hosted API customers, Redwood manages keys in cloud KMS (we provide key-splitting for high-sensitivity accounts). For Dedicated/Private, customers can deploy a customer-managed key with HSM or Redwood-managed broker.
- Cross-border: we support region pinning and an explicit data export approval flow for any cross-border transfer; that flow is in the procurement checklist.

I'll generate a short attestations bundle on EvidenceStore and share the link; Kimberly can confirm if Legal needs any extra exhibits.

—Ben
